title: Zenith Aisle: Workspace tethering + compact cost lens prototype
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: High-level redesign of the Console left rail and top routing to reduce cognitive overhead for multi-workspace users and surface cost and rollout controls without adding noise. Key idea: a compact 'Zenith Aisle' — a thin adaptive rail that tethers workspaces to a lightweight, hover-expand workspace card and exposes a persistent compact cost lens and rollout status badge. This ticket captures the prototype, usability findings, trade-offs with density vs discoverability, and next steps for engineering handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates workspace switch in <= 2 interactions for primary flows
Compact cost lens shows per-route token rate or spend delta on hover and matches Console backend metrics within 10%
Rollout control entry point is discoverable from three places: rail, route header, and command palette
Design tokens and spacing documented for responsive breakpoints (>= 1024px and mobile compact)
notes: Motivation: frequent workspace switching and route rollouts are leading to accidental context switching and hidden cost surprises in the existing left rail.

Core patterns explored: tethered hover card, compact cost lens (sparkline + delta), rollout hotspot (badge + quick-canary), command palette shortcut for fast switch (Cmd+K + workspace search), and keyboard-first nav (1..9 mapped favorites).
Accessibility: focus states kept within 4px visible ring, expand/collapse supports aria-expanded and aria-controls — verify with a11y team during handoff.
Performance: hover expansion should be purely client-side, minimal network fetch. Cost lens will use cached per-route aggregates; realtime detail available on click to fetch from metrics API.
comments: Marco Nguyen (PM) 2026-02-24: We need the rollout hotspot to be visible when there is an ongoing canary; stakeholders want immediate rollback access from the same surface.
Aisha Patel (Design) 2026-02-28: Updated prototype to include a tiny rollback action in the expanded card footer — flagged for security review because it maps to an action.
Leah Kim (Engineering) 2026-03-02: Suggest implementing the cost sparkline with a lightweight webworker to avoid jank on initial render. Will scope effort after design freeze.

Samir Rao (Research) 2026-03-06: Usability testing with eight participants (mix of platform engineers and PMs) — 6/8 completed primary task faster than baseline; common feedback: hover delay too sensitive on touchpads.
decisions: Adopt tethered hover card as primary compact workspace switcher for screens >= 1024px. Mobile uses full-screen workspace switcher modal.
Expose cost delta and 7-day sparkline in the compact lens; click expands to route cost panel served by metrics API.
Rollout hotspot remains visible for any route with active rollout percentage > 0 and surfaces quick actions (view details, pause, rollback) behind a confirmation modal.
Keyboard-first nav will be opt-in on user settings initially; default remains command-palette-driven switching.
usability_findings: Participants liked quick glance cost info but wanted clearer units (tokens vs $) — show both on hover in the expanded detail.
Hover-to-open needed 150ms debounce to avoid accidental expansions on cursor drift.
Favorites pins (first 4) were used heavily; users expect persistent ordering and drag-to-pin interactions.
Some users requested integration of route health (errors per minute) into the compact badge for high-risk routes.
tradeoffs: Density vs discoverability: making the rail thinner saved screen real estate but required hover and keyboard affordances for discoverability.
Client-side expansion limits network calls but increases client-responsibility for cached state; will require robust invalidation when workspace membership changes.
Rollout quick actions on hover increase risk of accidental operations; adding explicit confirmation mitigates but adds friction.
